episodes.199427: A potent shortwave trough dove southeastward from Missouri into the Tennessee Valley during the day and evening of April 10. Storms began firing over West Tennessee during the afternoon, moving southeasterly in conjunction with northwest flow aloft. Meanwhile, a pre-existing boundary was draped across north central Alabama, leftover from convection over Tennessee that morning. More storms began firing along this boundary during the late afternoon and evening hours, initially posing a hail threat. Up to golf ball-size hail fell across Etowah, Cherokee, and Blount counties, with steep mid-level lapse rates in place. Storms later grew upscale into a wind threat by sunset, with scattered pockets of wind damage across several counties.
episodes.199870: A squall line developed ahead of a cold front leading to wind damage in southeast NC.
episodes.199879: A squall line developed ahead of a front.
episodes.199886: Storm pulsed up to severe levels ahead of a strong upper trough.
episodes.199888: Storm pulsed up to severe levels ahead of a strong upper trough.
episodes.200114: A broad trough with embedded shortwave energy tracking across the region encountered a moderately unstable environment, leading to a line of showers and thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts across coastal waters.
episodes.200143: A cluster of supercells developed during the late afternoon hours, producing large hail at several locations in north central Alabama. The largest reported hail sized was 2.25 inches in Albertville in Marshall County. These storms also produced wind damage in northeast Alabama.  Then, a secondary batch of thunderstorms, merging at times with the original thunderstorms further south yielded a widespread swath of damaging winds from the northwest tip of Alabama, hard hitting the Shoals/Quad Cities metro area, then pushing through Morgan into Marshall Counties while another wave of wind spread from Madison through Jackson into DeKalb Counties.  Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in this swath, many landing on homes and vehicles, resulting in at least 3 injuries in the Sheffield, Decatur and Hartselle areas. Other more sporadic wind damage was reported further north. The damaging winds resulted in 20000-30000 without power for a period of time in northwest into north central Alabama. Around 250 damage reports were received from this event in north Alabama.
episodes.200688: Isolated severe storms developed with steep mid level lapse rates and moderate deep layer shear. Large hail was reported in Madison and Wakulla counties.
episodes.200725: An approaching cold front under a cold pool aloft producing steep lapse rates of just over 7 degC/km produced strong to severe hail storms.
episodes.200726: An approaching cold front under a cold pool aloft producing steep lapse rates of just over 7 degC/km produced strong to severe hail storms. Strong storm outflows pushed offshore over the local Atlantic waters.
episodes.201395: A mid to upper level trough combined with unusually low freezing heights, steep lapse rates, and enough CAPE to generate numerous reports of large hail during severe afternoon thunderstorms. Many reports, especially from the Knoxville metro, indicated the hail was a weird soft slush upon impact, with textures closer to graupel stones embedded in a snow mix, not a true ringed hailstone.
episodes.201759: An approaching cold front located over Hispaniola enhanced moisture content across the islands over the weekend. This lead to showery conditions and isolated thunderstorms, flooding was reported in San Juan and Barceloneta.
episodes.201847: A broken line of thunderstorms moved southward across north GA during the evening hours of April 10th. Robust CAPE and shear enabled storms to become strong to severe. The main event of the day was the splitting of one of the embedded cells. Left moving northern cell moved across the northern metro, generating significant and prolonged hail ranging from 1 to 2.5 inches in size. The right moving cell moved southeast across the southern metro, causing some hail up to 1 inch and widespread wind damage down through Macon. Other areas which experience large hail included the Dade, Walker and Catoosa counties as well as the Dawson county area.
episodes.202377: Scattered thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief severe weather in the mountains.
episodes.202380: Scattered thunderstorms developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. A couple of the storms produced hail.
episodes.202683: A round of storms moved across the north and northeast portions of the area. Some hail occurred with and area of quarter sized hail in northern Lowndes County.
episodes.203410: Scattered thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the afternoon. Some of the storms produced small hail.
episodes.204258: On the morning of the 10th, an area of low pressure was passing through the Ohio Valley, with a trailing cold front extending away from the low, back through southern Indiana and Illinois. As the day progressed this cold front slowly sank south and east across northern and central Kentucky. By 21Z a localized area of low pressure developed over west/central Kentucky, and by 00Z the cold front started to occlude over eastern Kentucky. With unstable air, and low freezing levels, and ample lift and cyclonic rotation, conditions were favorable for some hail development across eastern Kentucky.
